references.text: Refers to the importance of the words one speaks and their consequences, similar to Matthew 12:37 where words can justify or condemn.
James speaks about how the tongue is a small member but boasts of great things and has a major impact, paralleling how words can justify or condemn in Matthew 12:37.
David prays that the words from his mouth may be pleasing to God, which resonates with the idea that words can have positive or negative consequences as mentioned in Matthew 12:37.
Isaiah warns that the Lord will cleanse the lips of the people, which can be seen in connection with the significance of words and their power to justify or condemn as in Matthew 12:37.
The author of Hebrews speaks of God's word as living and powerful, emphasizing the importance of our words and their ability to justify or condemn, in line with Matthew 12:37.
